"Beauty Blender Pro" - A Smart Makeup Sponge Companion App

1. Project Overview & Core Vision

· Project Name: Beauty Blender Pro / The Sponge Society
· Core Vision: To create an end-to-end smart tool and community platform centered entirely around the makeup sponge. We will solve every user pain point through a closed-loop system of Smart Recommendation -> Professional Tutorials -> Cleaning Management -> Result Diagnosis -> Social Sharing -> Subscription Service, making foundation application simple, scientific, and enjoyable.

2. Target User Persona

· Primary Users: Makeup beginners, beauty enthusiasts, and young women experiencing "choice paralysis" and "technique anxiety."
· User Pain Points:
  · Selection Difficulty: Overwhelmed by different sponge shapes and materials.
  · Poor Technique: Incorrect application leads to patchy, cakey, or uneven foundation.
  · Maintenance Negligence: Cleaning is a hassle, leading to unhygienic, moldy tools.
  · Lack of Feedback: Inability to objectively evaluate their makeup result, leading to self-doubt.
  · Lack of Engagement: The makeup routine feels solitary, with no community for sharing or validation.

3. Detailed Core Feature Modules

Module 1: Smart Sponge Selector

· Objective: Use a personalized quiz to recommend the ideal makeup sponge, reducing decision fatigue.
· Implementation Logic:
  1. Users are prompted with a guided questionnaire upon opening the app.
  2. Questions include:
     · What is your skin type? (Dry / Oily / Combination / Normal)
     · What is your desired finish? (Dewy / Matte / Natural Satin)
     · What is your primary foundation formula? (Liquid / Cream / Stick / Cushion)
     · What is your biggest foundation concern? (Coverage / Longevity / Blendability)
  3. A backend algorithm (e.g., decision tree) processes the answers to output a recommendation including: Optimal Shape (teardrop, angled, etc.), Optimal Material (hydrophilic PU, latex-free, etc.), and a brief explanation linking the choice to their inputs.
· UI/UX Suggestion: Present questions as swipeable cards. The results page should feature a 3D rotatable view of the recommended sponge and its use-case scenarios.

Module 2: "Shape & Play" Tutorial Library

· Objective: Provide professional application tutorials focused on utilizing different parts of a makeup sponge.
· Content Structure:
  · By Area: Under-eye, Nose & Nostrils, Around the Mouth, Cheeks, Forehead.
  · By Technique: Stippling (bouncing), Patting, Rolling, Buffing/Polishing.
  · By Desired Finish: Natural "No-Makeup" Makeup, Full Coverage, Long-Lasting.
· Content Format: Short, sub-60-second videos + Step-by-step GIFs + Text summaries.
· Key Requirement: Videos/GIFs must clearly highlight the specific part of the sponge being used (e.g., "Use the PRECISION TIP," "Utilize the FLAT SIDE for polishing") with on-screen text and slow-motion replays to demonstrate technique nuances.

Module 3: "Sponge Care" Assistant

· Objective: Cultivate a habit of regular sponge cleaning to ensure tool hygiene.
· Sub-Features:
  · Usage Tracker & Cleaning Reminder: Users can log each use (or the app estimates frequency). After N uses (e.g., 5-7) or a set time period, a playful push notification is sent: "Your sponge needs a bath! 🛁"
  · Engaging Cleaning Tutorials: An IP character (e.g., "Spongey") demonstrates the standard cleaning process ("Wet, Lather, Rinse, Squeeze") via animated or live-action video.
  · Dry-Timer: After cleaning, users can start a countdown timer (default 4-8 hours, customizable). A notification at the end confirms: "Your sponge is fully dry and ready to use!"

Module 4: "Today's Look" AI Diagnosis

· Objective: Provide users with objective, quantitative feedback on their makeup to help them improve.
· Implementation Logic:
  1. User uploads a clear, well-lit photo of their face after makeup application.
  2. An AI image recognition engine analyzes the photo, focusing on:
     · Blendability & Smoothness (Caking, Patchiness)
     · Evenness (Color Uniformity)
     · Naturalism (Avoiding a "Mask-like" effect)
     · Detail Work (Around nose, eyes, pore coverage)
  3. Generates a Diagnostic Report: Provides an overall score (out of 100 or 5 stars) and breaks down the score by dimension with actionable, sponge-specific advice. Example: "Slight caking detected around your nostrils (see circled area). Next time, try prepping with more moisturizer and using your sponge's PRECISION TIP to press product into this area."

Module 5: IP Community - "The Blend"

· Objective: Build a user community to increase engagement and retention.
· Community Design:
  · Themed Challenges: Run official hashtags like #SpongeSavedMySkin, #BestBaseThisWeek, #CleanSpongeClub.
  · Content Format: Users can post photos or short videos of their looks, tips, before/after cleaning, etc.
  · Gamification: The IP character regularly features "Top Blenders of the Week," rewarding them with new sponges, cleanser, or merchandise. Include stand...1. Core Goal:
Implement a "Quarterly Refresh" subscription where users automatically receive a new sponge every 3 months. Manage the full lifecycle: subscription, payment, renewal, and notifications.

2. Detailed Requirements:

· A. Subscription Plan Display Page:
  · Page Title: "Quarterly Refresh Club" or similar.
  · Clearly display the plan: e.g., "Standard Plan - 1 curated sponge every 3 months - Price: $X/quarter".
  · Highlight benefits: "Exclusive early access", "Free shipping", "Cancel anytime".
· B. Subscription & Payment Flow:
  · User clicks "Subscribe Now" -> triggers the app's native payment flow (e.g., Apple App Store/Google Play Billing or Stripe).
  · On Successful Payment:
    1. Update the user's profile: set subscription_status to "active".
    2. Set subscription_start_date and calculate the next_shipment_date (current date + 3 months).
    3. Create the initial order record in the database.
· C. User Subscription Management Page:
  · Accessible via "My Account" or "Profile".
  · Display: Current status (active/cancelled), next_shipment_date, shipping address, order history.
  · Provide a "Cancel Subscription" button (stops future renewals but does not refund the current period).
· D. Backend Cron Job & Notifications (Server-Side):
  · Renewal & Shipping Job: Run a daily cron job to check for users where next_shipment_date is "today". For each:
    1. Charge for the new period (ensure payment method is valid).
    2. Create a new shipment order.
    3. Update next_shipment_date by adding another 3 months.
  · Push Notifications:
    · 7 days before next_shipment_date: "Your next sponge ships soon! Your card will be charged on [date]."
    · After order creation: "Your Quarterly Sponge has shipped! Track your order here."

---

Feature 2: Makeup Step Rhythm Timer

1. Core Goal:
Create an embedded timer for tutorials to help users time specific steps (e.g., letting primer set, masking), making the routine more professional and guided.

2. Detailed Requirements:

· A. Timer Component UI:
  · A visually prominent, circular countdown progress bar.
  · Large digital display in the center showing remaining time (MM:SS).
  · Three preset buttons below: 3 MIN, 5 MIN, 10 MIN. Tapping one starts the countdown immediately.
· B. Timer Interaction Logic:
  · On tap, the progress bar animates (fills or empties) as time counts down.
  · The active button changes to a "PAUSE" button. Tapping pauses/resumes.
  · On Timer End: The progress bar completes, the UI element pulses/vibrates briefly, and a gentle, non-intrusive sound plays.
  · Include a "RESET" button to stop and clear the current timer.
· C. Integration into Tutorials:
  · This should be a reusable component (e.g., RhythmTimer.vue for Vue or RhythmTimer.jsx for React).
  · Example call-to-action in a tutorial step: "After applying primer, start the 3-minute timer below to let it absorb fully before foundation." make the all images in app replacable

I'm now mapping out how different components will work together. I'm focusing on the `Shape & Play` library and the integration of features like the dry-timer in `SpongeCare`. I'm using `Gemini 2.5 Flash Image` for editing in the `ImageEditor` component. Moreover, I'm thinking about the structure, considering reusable elements and a service wrapper for `Gemini` API calls. I plan to use placeholder URLs for images until I can integrate the generation functionality.


**Refining API Integration**

I'm now fully immersed in the implementation of the `services/gemini.ts` file. I'm focusing on crafting a robust and efficient approach to interacting with the Gemini API, ensuring optimal performance and reliability for all AI-driven features. This file will form the bedrock of my application's AI functionality, so I'm paying meticulous attention to error handling, rate limiting, and request optimization.
